## The path from "issue goes overdue" to "assignee gets told, once"

**What starts the check.** An external scheduler (Vercel Cron or similar) hits `POST /api/cron/overdue/route.ts`, which calls `assertCronSecret(request)` to verify the caller, then calls `runOverdueIssueJob(new Date())` from `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`. That function wraps its body in `runJob("overdue-issues", ...)` (`src/server/jobs/types.ts`), which gives it a `JobResult` counter and standard error handling. This route is designed to be hit repeatedly on a short interval — the code comments call it "one pass" — so everything downstream has to cope with running every few minutes forever.

**How the set of issues is narrowed.** Inside `runOverdueIssueJob`, first `shouldFilterArchived(LIVE_ONLY)` (from `src/lib/soft-delete.ts`) is checked as a sanity guard — if archive scoping isn't configured correctly the sweep bails out entirely rather than risk querying archived rows. Then `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup(ORG_BATCH)` (`src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts`) fetches up to 50 organizations per pass, and for each org, `issueRepo.listOverdueIssues(orgId, stamp)` (`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts:507`) runs the actual filter: not archived, `dueAt` not null, `dueAt < now`, and status still one of `backlog`/`todo`/`in_progress`/`in_review` (so issues already `done` never count).

**What the job does and doesn't own.** For each qualifying issue, it skips anything already in an in-memory `reported` Set (keyed by issue id), then calls `emit("issue.overdue", {...})` from `src/lib/event-bus.ts`, passing `orgId`, `issueId`, `dueAt`, and `assigneeId`. Only on a successful emit does it add the issue id to `reported`. The job's own doc comment is explicit about the boundary: "The job owns no notification logic: it announces the fact, and whoever cares... reacts on the bus." So the job's responsibility ends at detecting overdue issues and publishing one event per issue; it has no idea who gets told, through what channel, or whether anything is muted.

**What stops repeat announcements.** The `reported` Set inside `overdue-issue-job.ts` is process-lifetime memory, not persisted state — but since the same server process keeps re-running this sweep every few minutes, that in-memory set is exactly what prevents the same still-open, still-overdue issue from generating a second `issue.overdue` event on the next pass. (A test-only `resetOverdueTracking()` exists to clear it between test scenarios.) There's a second, independent dedup layer further downstream for the email leg, described below.

**How it reaches one specific person.** `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` subscribes to the bus at module load via `registerFanOut()` → `subscribe("issue.overdue", ...)`. That handler checks `payload.assigneeId === null` and bails if there's no assignee (an overdue-but-unassigned issue announces nothing to a person); otherwise it calls `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [payload.assigneeId], {...})` — note the recipient list is a single-element array, so from here on exactly one user is in play.

Inside `notify()`, for that recipient it loads their stored delivery preference via `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "issue_overdue")` (`src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`), then calls `resolveChannels(preference, flags)` (`notification-service.ts:156`): no preference row means the default `["in_app", "email"]`; otherwise it's built from the user's own toggles — `inApp` and `email`, with `email` additionally gated by `digestOnly` (if `digestOnly` is set, the immediate email is suppressed) and the org's `digest_email` plan flag via `isEnabled()`. If the resolved channel list is empty (user muted everything), that recipient is skipped with no row written at all. Otherwise `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` (`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`) writes one row carrying the chosen `channels` — this is the row that shows up in that user's in-app inbox (surfaced through `notification-store.ts` / `use-notifications.ts` / `notification-list.tsx`).

The "email" channel isn't sent synchronously here — it's picked up later by a second cron-triggered job, `runDigestEmailJob` in `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts` (triggered via `src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts`), which only processes each org during its configured `digestHourUtc` (`shouldRunForOrg`), so each org gets swept once per day rather than once per tick. For each recipient it calls `buildDigest`/`renderDigest` (`digest-service.ts`) to bundle unread email-channel notifications and `sendEmail` (`email-service.ts`, which in this offline corpus just logs the draft rather than making network calls) to deliver it. Immediately after sending, it calls `notificationRepo.markRead` on every bundled notification — this is the second dedup layer, ensuring the same overdue notice can't be swept into a future digest and emailed again, independent of the job-level `reported` Set that stops the event itself from re-firing.
